text:
**Card spending: no Monzo fee.** When you pay abroad with your UK Monzo debit card, Monzo uses Mastercard’s exchange rate without adding a fee. If a shop offers to charge you in pounds, **choose the local currency** so you don’t get the shop’s exchange rate instead. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees?trk=public_post_comment-text))

**Cash withdrawals: it depends on your account and where you withdraw.** These are Monzo’s fee-free allowances per rolling 30 days. If you go over your allowance, Monzo charges **3% on the amount over it**. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees?trk=public_post_comment-text))

| Your Monzo personal account | UK and European Economic Area (EEA) | Outside the UK and EEA |
|---|---:|---:|
| Free account — not your main bank | £400 | £200 |
| Free account — your main bank | Unlimited | £200 |
| Extra | Unlimited | £200 |
| Plus | Unlimited | £400 |
| Premium, Perks or Max | Unlimited | £600 |

The EEA includes all EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. You can check your remaining allowance in the Monzo app under **your account → ⋯ → Fees and allowances**. Even within your allowance, the ATM operator may charge a separate fee. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees?trk=public_post_comment-text))
